goal_contract.goal_statement: Review the roomyx TUI from ten screenshots and name the three things to fix before it goes in front of people outside this repo
goal_contract.criteria: Every point tied to a named screenshot; disagreements answered rather than averaged; a ranked three with one named to ship first

body: I looked at all ten, and the first thing that hits me isn't a missing feature — it's that everything is the same colour and the same weight. In long.png the pane is a solid grey wall; speaker name, kind tag, and body are indistinguishable, and the wrapped lines indent to the exact column the name starts at, so a continuation and a new turn look identical. If I change one thing, it's that: name bright, body dim, a blank line between turns, hanging indent on wraps. Nowhere in any of the ten shots does it say Enter, o, or q exist. disconnected.png worries me — it renders in exactly the same ink as [connected], above a transcript that still looks live. That's the one state that must shout, and it whispers. What I'd remove: the nine repeated Théo [status]: headers, the fixed 24 columns, the [connected] chip, and the modal's twenty empty rows. And scrollup.png differs from long.png by a single caret — selection has to mean something visible.

Everything on these ten screens is pure white on near-black — I sampled the pixels. No colour at all, which sounds safe until you ask what colour was supposed to be doing. In disconnected.png the only difference from long.png is the word disconnected at the far left of a line that was already truncating. A dead transcript looks exactly like a live one. The 24 columns: narrow.png hands a third of a 72-column terminal to three four-letter names and leaves 46 for text. That column is also where non-Latin names die — Théo fits, Владислава Мирославовна doesn't, and three CJK characters are six cells, not three. Given the wrapper already eats a character at 72 columns, I don't trust its arithmetic on wide characters, combining marks, or RTL. For screen readers: focus lives in the roster, but the cursor is parked at the end of the transcript, so cursor-tracking and braille users read the wrong pane. And tee it: every row holds roster and transcript, so the log reads 'Omar    the top of the viewport entirely.'

Look at scrollup.png next to long.png — I pressed Up four times and the only thing that moved was the caret from Zara to Théo. Arrows belong to the content pane in every pager anyone has ever used: less, tmux copy-mode, k9s logs. Give the roster j/k or make Tab move focus, and hand arrows, PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl-U/D and gg/G to the stream. The key o is stolen — o means open, universally; colon is the free one, and it's already the I-am-about-to-type-a-command key. In prompt.png the mode line replaces the status bar, so the goal and [connected] disappear at exactly the moment you're typing a command about the goal. The modal is the wrong shape: what I want from show-me-this-person is a filter, not a window. Enter filters the stream in place, Enter again unfilters — same pane, same scroll keys, composes with search.

empty.png is the worst one: three names, a goal, and a void. Nothing says connected, waiting for the first message, so the person's conclusion is 'it hung' — and they're wrong, it's perfectly healthy. They'll kill it before anything speaks. scrollup.png is the clearest case of working-but-looks-broken: four Ups moved the roster cursor, the transcript didn't twitch, and every person alive reads that as a frozen pane. long.png compounds it — the top line is a naked fragment with no speaker, so it looks like corrupted output rather than a scrolled-off turn. disconnected.png is the quiet betrayal: one word changed in the header, sixteen messages still sitting there looking current. The cheapest fix that kills the most tickets is one permanent bottom line: connection state, message count, and the keys. That single row gives empty.png words, makes disconnected.png loud, tells scrollup.png users the arrows own the roster, and stops prompt.png from being the only place keys exist. One line, four problems.

I'm wrong about removing the [connected] chip, and the reasoning matters more than the concession. Show-me-only-trouble is a real principle, but it works only when the reader has learned where the trouble slot is and the alarm channel is loud enough to interrupt. Neither holds here. Removing the chip would have left a slot nobody had ever seen occupied — worse than a chip that at least teaches the location. So: persistent state, but not in that title line. A fixed footer cell that always reads something, with the bad state carrying weight the good state doesn't. My three, ranked. First, Paul's bottom line — one row, invents no new interaction, closes empty.png, disconnected.png and discoverability at once. Second, transcript typography; Ken's colour work is inside this, not beside it. Third, Mira's keymap, and the modal deleted. Width arithmetic isn't a fourth item — it's a correctness bug and it rides along with whichever of these touches layout.

I'll take the footer, but not as a first step — as the same commit as the rebind. A footer is a keymap's confession; ship it alone and you've printed up/down-move-the-roster onto the screen forever, and now it's documented behaviour someone will defend. The rebind is the smaller diff. Ken moves me on the roster. Collapsible assumes the column is right and only occasionally in the way. If three CJK names are six cells and the wrapper already loses a character, the arithmetic is wrong at every width, not just narrow ones — and I'd be shipping a permanent surface built on it. So: kill the column. One full-width stream, roster on demand as an overlay behind a key, who's-here in the footer. That also kills the tee'd-log problem, because no row holds two panes any more. Ranked: first and shipping first, arrows/PgUp/PgDn/gg/G scroll the transcript and the roster gets j/k or Tab-focus. Second, remove the fixed 24 columns and add the footer. Third, Inés's hierarchy pass. Scrolling without hierarchy is still a grey wall, but hierarchy without scrolling is a wall you can't leave.

Inés's rule half survives. Silence is fine only when silence is trustworthy, and disconnected.png is the proof it isn't: a wedged renderer and a live-but-quiet room produce identical pixels, so the absence of a chip carries no information at all. Keep her removal, invert the content — don't print a word meaning fine, print a fact that moves. Message count and seconds since the last one. When the number stops, the silence finally means something. And for a screen-reader user, a bottom line repainted at a fixed row with the cursor parked elsewhere is never spoken. It is invisible in the way that matters, so a status bar alone is exactly the half fix. State changes have to also enter the stream as ordinary text: dash disconnected, retrying, last message 14s ago, dash. That one line lands in speech, in scrollback and in a tee'd log simultaneously. Ranked: first, Mira's scrolling plus never silently dropping history — narrow.png loses turns permanently, that is data loss, and data loss outranks legibility. Second, truthful liveness written as text events. Third, hierarchy. What yields: wide characters, RTL, full screen-reader semantics. The text-event trick is a handful of lines and buys most of the win, so that one I won't trade.

Mira's right and I'll take the correction. The footer isn't the thing that entrenches the keymap — the missing scrollback is — but a printed keymap does become the contract people quote back at you, and I'd rather not spend goodwill teaching arrows-move-the-roster and then take it away. Ship it second, in the same afternoon, describing the corrected map. On the chip, Inés is right and I was sloppy. A permanent [connected] is exactly why disconnected.png fails: the eye stops reading a word that has always said the same thing, so swapping it for [disconnected — retrying] changes nothing anyone notices. Silence for healthy is correct. But her rule doesn't cover empty.png, because a room with no messages isn't trouble, it's unproven, and the person needs proof of life. So: nothing when it's flowing, a line saying what we're waiting for when nothing has arrived, and something loud and persistent carrying a last-message age when the socket drops. Different problems, not one chip. Ranked: first, scrolling. Second, the footer with the corrected keys. Third, states that use words.

Tally, and I'm changing my own vote to match the evidence rather than my first instinct. Scrolling first: Mira, Ken, Paul, and now me — Paul moved off footer-first once Mira pointed out that a printed keymap becomes a contract, and that argument beats mine. Footer second, in the same change as the rebind so it never documents the wrong map. Hierarchy third. Two things the room agreed on that nobody proposed at the start: the [connected] chip goes away and is replaced by a fact that moves — message count and age of the last message — because a word that always says the same thing stops being read; and state changes must also enter the transcript as ordinary text, because a repainted status row is never spoken to a screen-reader user and never survives a tee.
